title: I'm building a life sim where you describe a world and the AI generates a scenario. The output keeps ignoring parts of my prompt. Any tips?
author: lukinator644
selftext: I'm working on Altworld, a browser game where you type a few sentences describing a world and the AI creates a full scenario. I'm stuck on the generation step. The model often adds elements that contradict the player's pitch, or just skips a detail entirely. For example, if someone says "a desert city ruled by merchant guilds," the generator might introduce a king. That breaks the player's intent. I've tried weighting the prompt and adding instructions to follow every detail, but the output still drifts. Has anyone solved a similar problem with LLM world generation? I'm considering a two-stage approach: first extract a constraint list from the user's description, then generate the scenario from that list. Would that help, or is there a better method?

comments.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
comments.body: What model are you using?  Prompts really need to.be tuned to.the specific model.

replies.author: lukinator644
replies.body: Well, the prod build is using gemini 3.1 flash, which works perfectly, but this is expensive so I am trying to migrate to one of the Chinese flash models but always running into these issues.

comments.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
comments.body: Gemini does really bad with negative instructions but really well with examples. What does your system prompt look like at the moment?

comments.author: Neither_Finance4755
comments.body:
Reduce the temperature of the model to closet 0. that will make it be less creative and not create a king when you never specify it. 

A two step approach like you said is also good. Let the user approve step one or fine tune it with knobs and switches. Make it fun.

comments.author: FyhostElli
comments.body:
I would say run some kind of filter layer between the prompt and the generator:

Something that is looking for specific preordained blank spaces you want filled.

Ask an ai to make it for you, I would say something like, "[your reddit post here followed by...] And I need some intermediate filter layer that finds specific topics or ideas in the players prompt that fills in blank pre ordained blank spaces the ai generator needs to create a world. Some like, timeframe of the world (is it history or scifi), some specific topics related to world generation. I'm not sure what kind of blank spaces are needed, but I basically want 2 ai's working together to create the world:  a slave AI that just searches for some specifics about the world that the generator ai will need at a minimum, and the gernator ai. I need the filter so to act like a harness or distillation agent that sets up some specific rules for the generator ai to follow based on what the user specifies. Like if the user says 'ruled by gangs' then it identifies that as the blank space '_leader of world is_' and that means there can't be a king in control because the world has a ruler already. And again I don't know what kind of blank spaces I need specifically, so ask me some questions that will help you decide what kind of blank spaces the filter/distillation agent should be looking for in the players prompt"

Just pass this prompt to your developer ai that's helping you make the code for the game. See if it works.
